value.title: Cross-model review round 2 — pij-rs-send-defaults
value.note:
SEAT NOTE. The packet names the reviewer seat as pij-panicky-pheasant (legacy) / pij-moral-whale (rs-derived); this round was executed by pij-yearling-earwig. Flagged to the PM at ack. The two ids in the reviewer field are the SAME process (pid 94823, proc_start 20260902150558) named differently by the legacy store and the rs store — which is not trivia, it is F5.

SCOPE. Read-only on code. Nothing outside assets/reviews/ was written. The production daemon (127.0.0.1:7461, pid 46147) was never stopped, restarted, or written to; it was confirmed still running on the same pid after teardown. Every live probe ran against an ISOLATED daemon I started myself on 127.0.0.1:17931 with its own state dir under a scratchpad, with one throwaway registered peer, all torn down afterwards.

EVIDENCE I RAN MYSELF (i7 — the author's receipts and assets/live-send-defaults.md were treated as hypotheses throughout; nothing below is quoted from them). cargo test --workspace: 591 passed, 0 failed, across the run — independently reproducing the AC5 receipt figure exactly. cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings: exit 0, read as a BARE exit status rather than through a pipe. cargo build -p pij-cli: exit 0. LIVE probes on the isolated daemon: pane-derived adopt; derived send with no --from/--msg-id; contradictory PIJ_SESSION_ID on BOTH send and report; missing body; absent identity; cross-seat destructive refusal; cross-seat --peek with NO actor identity at all; repeated peek idempotence; and a byte-level body comparison by SHA-256.

AC LEDGER (d1 — every AC judged with evidence).
AC1 TRUE. On the isolated daemon, `pij-rs send --to pij-probe-peer --body hello` with PIJ_SESSION_ID unset and no --from/--msg-id returned `ok` with meta `from pij-yodelling-sniper; msg_id 01a0608c-0c3b-76a1-b070-ed527e202f33` — sender derived from the pane, id minted, and the minted id echoed in the receipt as G2 requires. The id parses as UUIDv7 (version nibble 7 at the expected offset).
AC2 TRUE, and proven at the byte level rather than by inspection. Three bodies were sent and then drained from the recipient's own inbox, and each was SHA-256 compared against the source: the hostile stdin payload `--not-a-flag body with $(danger) and `backticks`` (48 bytes, 5a37135ebc890173), a `--body` value beginning with a hyphen (20 bytes, 4b0d3982e53a26fd), and a 5120-byte file (5dd703e5e3d2af68). All three hashes matched the source exactly. Nothing was shell-expanded and no leading hyphen was parsed as a flag.
AC3 TRUE — the round-1 headline defect is genuinely closed. Sitting in a pane owned by `pij-yodelling-sniper` while asserting `PIJ_SESSION_ID=pij-yearling-earwig`: `send` refused with `the caller claims to be pij-yearling-earwig but pane %3168 belongs to pij-yodelling-sniper — refusing rather than answering for either`, and `report` refused with the identical text. Both exit 1, read bare. Missing body refuses by name (`missing message body: pass --body <text> or --body-file <path|->`) with exit 1 and NO usage dump, satisfying G3/req-0032. Absent pane and absent env refuses naming both inputs, exit 1. The CLI's second ladder is gone: `resolve_acting_seat` now sends seat AND pane together and lets the daemon rule, which is the fix round-1 F1 asked for.
AC4 PARTLY TRUE — see F6. The pointer half is true: `render_pointer` and `render_final_pointer` say `pij inbox check`, with tests pinning the exact strings. The pane-bound adopt half is true and now genuinely covers omp/pi: `adopt_tells_pane_bound_harnesses_that_the_pane_resolves_identity` loops over claude/copilot/codex/omp/pi and asserts the meta names the pane and contains no export line — closing round-1 F4. Live adopt of my own pane returned `adopted pij-yodelling-sniper; identity resolves from pane %3168 on each command — no PIJ_SESSION_ID export is required for this harness`. The clause that is NOT true is the last one, `paneless seats retain export advice`: no reachable surface emits it. That is F6.
AC5 TRUE, independently. cargo test --workspace 591 passed / 0 failed, matching the receipt's figure exactly; clippy -D warnings exit 0. The two req-0044 baseline reds are TypeScript and outside the Rust workspace, so they were correctly out of this run rather than suppressed within it.
AC6 TRUE — round-1 F2 closed. `pij-rs inbox --seat pij-probe-peer` from a different acting seat refuses naming both ids (exit 1) before any claim. `--peek --seat <other>` with BOTH PIJ_SESSION_ID and TMUX_PANE unset succeeds and returns the body — the operator/debug path round-1 flagged as lost is restored, and the CLI now correctly skips the identity ladder entirely when peek is paired with an explicit seat. Peeking twice returned the same msg_id, and round-1 F3's unwitnessed guard now has a real witness: `peek_inbox_preserves_delivery_and_rejects_misdirected_payloads` covers the misdirected-payload refusal, and the HTTP test asserts the spine carries no INBOX_ACK_EVENT_KIND after a peek — the negative assertion round-1 asked for and did not have.

ROUND-1 RE-JUDGEMENT (i8 — re-judged against the new code, not re-reported). F1 FIXED (verified live on send and report). F2 FIXED (verified live: paneless cross-seat peek works). F3 FIXED (verified by reading the two new tests, including the negative spine assertion). F4 FIXED (verified: the harness list became `pane.is_some()` and the test loops omp/pi). No round-1 finding is carried forward.

COMPOSITION SEAMS (d2). (1) CLI-to-daemon identity: the seam round-1 broke on. Now single-ladder — `resolve_acting_seat` sends both inputs, `resolve_seat` decides, and the CLI adds only an equality check of an explicit --from/--seat against the daemon's answer. Traced and exercised live on three verbs. This seam is sound in isolation and is where F5 lives at the deployment layer. (2) peek: CLI --peek to `?peek=true` to `DeliveryService::peek_inbox` to `Queue::peek`, traced end to end, exercised live, and witnessed by a shared queue contract that runs over BOTH FakeQueue and SqliteQueue — with all three of peek's deliberate divergences from claim mirrored identically in the fake, so the contract is not vacuous. (3) msg-id minting versus daemon dedupe: unchanged from round 1 and still sound. (4) Verb coverage of G1: this is where drift remains — F7.

FLOWSPACE DOGFOOD (i1). `flowspace3 search 'resolve acting seat identity from tmux pane'` returned `crates/cli/src/main.rs::resolve_command_seat` as the top hit (score 0.765, semantic channel), which is exactly the function this round's identity judgement rests on. FRICTION, and it is the same one round 1 reported and nobody has fixed: the `flowspace` skill documents `flowspace3 search "<concept>" --mode semantic`, and this build still rejects `--mode` outright with `error: unexpected argument '--mode' found`. A reviewer following the skill text verbatim gets a hard failure on their first search. Semantic appears to be the default, so the fix is skill-side.

value.finding:
HIGH. The plan removed the only escape hatch from identity resolution without providing a replacement, and the resulting refusal is unrecoverable for a whole class of live seats. Before this plan, `pij-rs send` took `--from: String` and passed it straight into `SendRequest` with no resolution at all; a seat whose environment and pane disagreed could still send by naming itself. Now `resolve_command_seat` runs the ladder UNCONDITIONALLY, before and independently of any `--from`, so a contradicted seat cannot send or report at all — and passing the correct `--from` does not help, because the ladder has already refused by the time the assertion is compared. The refusal is correct POLICY and I am not asking for it to be relaxed; the defect is that it names no recovery, and the composition it lands in produces the contradiction as a matter of course rather than as an attack.

The reason it is routine rather than exceptional: rs derives a seat name for a pane via `allocate_memorable_id(registry, seed)` (crates/daemon/src/http/mod.rs:405) seeded by the PANE, taking the first candidate free in that store. The legacy CLI mints its own name independently. So one process acquires two names, and they will essentially never coincide. I verified the determinism rather than inferring it: a FRESH isolated daemon with a provably empty roster (`{"seats":[]}`), adopting my pane, minted `pij-yodelling-sniper` — the identical name the production store already held for that pane. Same seed, same candidate order, same answer, in two unrelated stores.
value.note:
PROOF — this review's own first command was the reproduction, before I had read any code.

  $ pij send pij-conscious-elephant --body-file <ack>
  E-RS: send: rs at 127.0.0.1:7461 FAILED — not falling back to legacy (the caller claims to be `pij-yearling-earwig` but pane `%3168` belongs to `pij-yodelling-sniper` — refusing rather than answering for either. An asserted id never outranks an observable one.)

The two names are ONE process, and the pair the schema itself calls identity matches exactly: tmux reports pane %3168 has pane_pid 94823; `ps -o lstart -p 94823` gives Wed 2 Sep 15:05:58 2026; and the rs row is `pij-yodelling-sniper|%3168|94823|20260902150558|idle`. Both pid AND proc_start agree, so this is NOT the recycled-pid false-positive that a pid-only check would produce — it is genuinely one live process under two names. The legacy store and PIJ_SESSION_ID say `pij-yearling-earwig`; the rs store says `pij-yodelling-sniper`.

Aggravating: the diagnostic surfaces do not participate. `pij whoami` and `pij phonehome` both answer `pij-yearling-earwig` cheerfully — phonehome even reports `(bound)` — because they resolve from legacy, while `send`/`report` resolve from rs. An operator asking the platform who it is gets one answer, and the verb that acts gets another. A surface that reports identity while a different authority governs it is exactly the failure this repo has paid for before.

SMALLEST FIX (two parts, the second is the cheap one and I would take it alone if only one lands): (a) make the refusal recoverable by naming the gesture, since the caller cannot derive it — the adopt path already accepted this principle when it was fixed to hand back the id as `the one thing the caller cannot derive`; the send/report refusal should append the equivalent, e.g. `— this shell's PIJ_SESSION_ID names a different store's id; re-run as `env -u PIJ_SESSION_ID pij-rs send …` or re-adopt this pane`. I verified that `env -u PIJ_SESSION_ID` does in fact restore full function on every affected verb, so the advice is real and testable, not speculative. (b) Have `whoami`/`phonehome` resolve through the same authority as `send`/`report`, or say plainly which store answered. Assert the two answers equal in a test, so the diagnostic cannot drift from the behaviour again.

NOT ASKED FOR: relaxing the guard, or preferring the asserted id. The posture is right; only its recoverability and its diagnostic honesty are missing.

value.finding: MEDIUM — a plan promise that is not true, which is priority (1) on the packet's ordering. AC4 and G4 both end with the clause that export advice survives for paneless seats (`export advice is paneless-only`, `paneless seats retain export advice`), and AC4 is checked [x]. The branch that would emit it is unreachable. `adopt` computes `resolves_from_pane = pane.is_some()` at line 518, but at line 457 — a hundred lines EARLIER — it has already returned `refused(...)` whenever `pane` is `None`. Control therefore reaches line 557 only when `pane.is_some()`, so `resolves_from_pane` is invariably `true` and the `else` arm holding the export text is dead code. The advice was not made paneless-only; it was made unreachable. Nothing distinguishes those two states from the outside, which is precisely why the AC reads as satisfied.
value.note:
PROOF, at three levels.
(1) Source: the early `return refused(ADOPT, "adopt registers a seat from evidence the daemon can DERIVE, and with no pane there is nothing to derive from…")` at identity.rs:457 precedes the `resolves_from_pane` computation at :518 and dominates every path to :557.
(2) Live, on the isolated daemon: `env -u TMUX_PANE pij-rs adopt --harness claude` returns exactly that refusal. There is no paneless adopt to carry the advice.
(3) Repo-wide: `grep -rn 'export PIJ_SESSION_ID' crates/` returns exactly two lines — the dead branch at identity.rs:564, and identity_tests.rs:806, which asserts the NEGATIVE (`!meta.contains("export PIJ_SESSION_ID")`). So the only surviving occurrence of the string in the product is unreachable, and the only test that mentions it proves it is absent. No test covers the else arm; consistent with round-1's own `witness` doctrine, it is a branch that could be deleted with nothing going red.

Why it is worth a finding rather than a nit: a genuinely paneless seat — the `register` path, which adopt's own refusal text points callers to — still NEEDS PIJ_SESSION_ID, because `resolve_acting_seat` has nothing else to work from without a pane. So the guidance is not obsolete, it is missing for the one population that requires it. Partial mitigation, stated in fairness: the `no acting seat` refusal does mention setting PIJ_SESSION_ID, so a paneless caller is not left with nothing — but that is a refusal encountered after failure, not the guidance at registration the AC claims.

SMALLEST FIX (PM's call): either move the export line to the `register` response, where the paneless population actually is, and reword AC4/G4 to say so; or delete the dead arm and amend AC4/G4 to drop the paneless clause. Both are honest; leaving AC4 checked with the clause unbacked is not. Amend by excision rather than by appending a caveat, so the guide and the AC do not end up with two authoritative halves.

value.finding:
MEDIUM, interface drift from G1 — reported with an explicit scoping caveat so the PM can rank it fairly. G1 promises that EVERY pij-rs verb needing the acting seat derives it and refuses contradiction; the impl-guide directs the coder to `find every `seat: Option<String>` / --from arg`. `SidecarAction::Telegram` still declares `from: String`, `body: String` and `msg_id: String` as mandatory, unresolved, unvalidated arguments — the exact boilerplate this plan exists to delete, on a verb that both sends and needs the acting seat. It never calls `resolve_command_seat`, so the anti-impersonation posture the plan establishes has a hole one verb over.

This matters slightly more than cosmetics because of what `--from` DOES there: its own doc comment says `Sending seat, which the inbound reply will route back to`. An asserted `--from` therefore does not merely mislabel an outbound message, it binds where Telegram's inbound replies are delivered — so a caller can redirect another seat's operator replies to itself by naming it, with no pane check anywhere on the path.
value.note:
PROOF: `grep -n 'resolve_command_seat' crates/cli/src/main.rs` returns four call sites — send, inbox (x2), report — and none in the sidecar arm. The declaration at main.rs:288-296 is unchanged by this branch (`git diff` touches it not at all), while its sibling `Send` variant at :211 was converted to `Option<String>` with full resolution.

SCOPING CAVEAT, stated plainly rather than buried: no AC names the sidecar verb. AC1-AC6 cover send, inbox, report, adopt and the pointer text only, and all six are judged on their own terms above. So this is drift from G1's wording and the impl-guide's instruction, NOT a failed AC, and the PM is entitled to rule it out of scope for this plan. I report it because G1 says `every`, because the impl-guide asked for the sweep explicitly, and because the reply-routing consequence makes it the one remaining unresolved `--from` that carries a real impersonation surface.

SMALLEST FIX: if in scope, make `from` `Option<String>` and route it through `resolve_command_seat(&client, "pij sidecar telegram", from.as_deref())` exactly as `send` does, and mint `msg_id` the same way. If out of scope, record it as a known-open row against req-0041 so the next reader does not re-derive it — per w2 this is named as a note for prime rather than an expansion of the review.

value.rationale: Reproduced by this review's own first command, before any code was read, and then re-derived from source rather than from the symptom. The one-process-two-names claim is corroborated on the full liveness PAIR (pid 94823 AND proc_start 20260902150558 both matching the rs row), which rules out the recycled-pid explanation. The determinism that makes it routine was verified experimentally, not assumed: a provably empty isolated store minted the identical name for the same pane. The recovery I propose was tested (`env -u PIJ_SESSION_ID` restores every affected verb), so the suggested refusal text is known-true advice.

Confirmed at three independent levels — source dominance of the early paneless refusal, a live paneless adopt returning that refusal, and a repo-wide grep showing the only product occurrence of the string is in the dead arm while the only test mentioning it asserts its absence. The AC clause is unbacked as written.

Confirmed as drift from G1 and from the impl-guide's explicit sweep instruction: four resolve_command_seat call sites exist and none is the sidecar arm, whose mandatory --from is untouched by this branch. Confirmed as drift only — no AC names this verb, and the PM may legitimately rule it out of scope for plan 130 without any AC becoming false.

Re-judged against the new code per i8, not re-reported. The CLI's second ladder is gone — resolve_acting_seat now sends seat and pane together and the daemon rules. Verified live on both send and report from a contradicted environment: each refuses by name, exit 1.

Verified live: with both PIJ_SESSION_ID and TMUX_PANE unset, --peek with an explicit --seat returns the body. The CLI now skips the ladder entirely for that combination, restoring the paneless operator read while the destructive cross-seat form still refuses.

Both halves closed. peek_inbox_preserves_delivery_and_rejects_misdirected_payloads witnesses the previously unwitnessed misdirected-payload guard, and the HTTP inbox test now asserts NEGATIVELY that the spine carries no INBOX_ACK_EVENT_KIND after a peek — the no-evidence assertion round 1 asked for by name.

The stale harness allowlist became a structural test (pane.is_some()), so the question of which harnesses are pane-bound no longer has a hand-maintained answer that can rot. adopt_tells_pane_bound_harnesses_that_the_pane_resolves_identity loops claude/copilot/codex/omp/pi and asserts no export line, and live adopt confirmed the text.
